handoff: 1 blocking finding, about the AC3 merge case. pushBranch pushes the branch and the forced heads ref without --atomic, so after a rejected push and a failed take-in the heads ref moves alone and diverges from the branch. A takeover then takes the branch and drops the boundary instead of merging. AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC5 are met; tests are green.

findings.title: A non-atomic push can leave the heads ref diverged from the branch, and takeover then drops the boundary instead of merging
findings.detail:
AC3: 'when another machine takes the story over, then it resumes from the heads ref merged with the remote branch (never rebased)'. checkout.ts:272 (aheadOf) uses the heads ref only when the remote branch is its ancestor. Otherwise it takes refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch> as before, and nothing merges the two. The handoff argues that before a PR the two refs only diverge on a rewrite. That is false because of push.ts:394-395. git.push sends `refs/heads/<b>:refs/heads/<b>` and `+refs/heads/<b>:refs/norn/heads/<story>` without --atomic. When a person pushed to the story branch, git rejects the branch refspec as non-fast-forward but still updates the forced heads ref to the local boundary. pushBranch then calls takeRemoteBranch (push.ts:398). When that merge conflicts or fails (push.ts:73-76), it returns an error with the remote holding branch = the person's commit and heads ref = the boundary, diverged. If the holder crashes now, a takeover sees aheadOf false, takes the person's branch, and the boundary is missing from B's worktree. That is the work loss AC3 is meant to prevent, and AC1's 'in one push' does not hold either: half of the push landed. No test covers a diverged heads ref (heads-ref.test.ts only makes the branch lag behind the heads ref).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Push the branch and heads ref atomically (`git push --atomic`: add an `atomic` option to GitPort.push or always pass it for several refspecs, with a contract test that a rejected branch refspec leaves the heads ref unmoved). Then the heads ref never moves without the branch, and before a PR only a rewrite can diverge them. Alternatively, implement the merge at takeover for a diverged heads ref. Either way, add an integration test for the rejected-push-then-crash case.
